parameters.excerpt: The floating-point registers are now extended to hold either a single, double, or quad-precision floating-point value (FLEN=128).
parameters.reasoning: FLEN=128 is a direct implementation parameter that defines the width of floating-point registers when the Q extension is implemented. This is a design-time choice that affects the register file architecture.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: FLQ and FSQ are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned and XLEN=128.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This describes a conditional guarantee about atomic execution based on alignment and XLEN value. It is a behavioral specification, not an implementation choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: FLQ and FSQ do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This is a fixed requirement that all implementations must satisfy. There is no implementation choice - all implementations must preserve NaN payloads.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: FCVT.L[U].Q and FCVT.Q.L[U] are RV64-only instructions.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This states which instructions are available in RV64 vs RV32. It is a fixed architectural rule based on the base ISA, not an implementation parameter.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: FMV.X.Q and FMV.Q.X instructions are not provided in RV32 or RV64, so quad-precision bit patterns must be moved to the integer registers via memory.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This states that certain instructions are not provided in any current base ISA. It is a fixed architectural limitation, not an implementation choice.
